offering_description.value: Provides inspection and asset integrity services to industrial operators. It also delivers engineering, environmental consulting and geospatial services to utilities, infrastructure owners and government agencies through field crews, laboratories and technical specialists.

primary_products.value: Geospatial imagery analysis and remote sensing software

primary_services.value: Nondestructive testing and inspection; engineering and infrastructure consulting; geospatial surveying and mapping; rope-access maintenance; environmental consulting

customer_segment.value: B2B: Industrial plant operators, energy producers, utilities and commercial property owners; B2G: Transportation departments, public works agencies and federal mapping agencies

end_markets.value: Oil and gas; power and utilities; transportation infrastructure; manufacturing; commercial buildings

revenue_model.value: project or contract: Inspection and maintenance programs, infrastructure design and mapping projects; service fees: Field inspections, laboratory tests and specialist consulting; licensing or royalties: Geospatial imagery processing and analysis software licenses
revenue_model.category: project or contract; service fees; licensing or royalties

value_chain_position.value: service provider: Uses field measurements, samples and site data to deliver testing, engineering and mapping to asset owners and agencies; software / platform: Provides tools for businesses and public agencies to analyze satellite and aerial imagery

geography_served.value: global: Primarily the United States and Canada, with operations in selected international markets, including Asia

specialization.value: related lines: Industrial asset integrity, infrastructure engineering, environmental consulting and geospatial technology

distribution_channels.value: direct sales: Account teams, competitive bids and public procurement contracts

regulatory_exposure.value: high: Industrial radiography requires radiation licenses, and state and provincial boards regulate professional engineering practice.

notes: The current scope of the geospatial software business and the full list of countries served are uncertain.
